newsitem.title: CHINA: China March RPI up 1.7 pct yr/yr - state statistics.
newsitem.headline: China March RPI up 1.7 pct yr/yr - state statistics.

text.p: China's retail price inflation rose 1.7 percent in March compared with the year-ago period, the Xinhua news agency quoted the State Statistical Bureau as saying.
Retail price inflation was 2.9 percent in February and 3.3 percent in January.
The figure for the first quarter was 2.6 percent, lower than an estimate by Premier Li Peng this week that benchmark retail price inflation would average 3.0 percent in January-March.
Although inflation has eased considerably, a statement from the bureau said government departments should monitor the services sector where price rises have been somewhat higher.
China has said it would be able to curb inflation below 6.0 percent this year.

Retail price inflation in 1996 was 6.1 percent, compared with 14.8 percent in 1995 and a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994. First-quarter retail price inflation in 13 of China's 29 provinces and municipalities was below the national average, the figures showed.

The lowest inflation was in Shanghai, which reported inflation of 1.0 percent for the first quarter, while the rate in southwestern Sichuan province was 5.8 percent and in Beijing was 5.5 percent for the first three months.
